title: Mirabel and the Compass
premise: In 1899, Juniper Lockridge, a pearl diver's child indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has survived two decades by mastering strategic silence. When an abandoned child arrives at their door clutching a brass compass and a ledger page that implicates the company's founders in a decades-old drowning, Juniper must choose between the safety of forgetting and the danger of remembering. Smuggling the evidence past three checkpoints—harbor, customs house, and company archive—before the century turns forces Juniper to confront the mother they were made to forget. The book ends as the clock strikes midnight on January 1, 1900: the ledger reaches a magistrate's hands, the child is claimed by kin rather than the company, and Juniper, finally speaking their mother's name aloud, walks free of their contract into an uncertain but self-owned future.
about_author: Ines Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing colonial shipping records in coastal Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. They write about the people history files under 'miscellaneous cargo.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A night dive gone wrong establishes Juniper's world: debt ledgers, the company's watchful foreman, and the silences that keep divers alive. The emotional beat is weary competence masking old grief over a mother lost to the sea—or so Juniper was told.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. During a monsoon night, a six-year-old named Sefa appears at Juniper's door with a brass compass and a torn ledger page, along with a note: forget the face that left her. The beat is fear curdling into recognition—the handwriting is familiar.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, with Sefa listening. By lamplight Juniper deciphers the page: it records a 'write-off'—a diver declared drowned while still alive, her contract sold. The date matches the year Juniper's mother vanished. Beat: vertigo; the ground of Juniper's identity shifts.

chapters.title: The Foreman's Kindness
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Company foreman Aldous Wren shows unexpected generosity—a food ration, a warning about 'troublemakers.' Juniper realizes kindness here is surveillance. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve; Sefa must be hidden.

chapters.title: Lessons in Forgetting
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, childlike and precise. Sefa recounts fragments: a woman's face, a boat, being told to forget. She practices forgetting like a chore and fails. Beat: heartbreaking innocence that mirrors Juniper's own trained amnesia back at them.

chapters.title: The Harbor Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. First attempt to move the ledger page out via a sympathetic boatwright stalls when harbor guards announce new century-turn inspections. Beat: first real obstacle; Juniper learns the company expects exactly this kind of smuggling.

chapters.title: Old Debts, Older Names
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper seeks out retired diver Maren Okonkwo, who once dove beside Juniper's mother. Maren confirms the write-off scheme and gives a name: the magistrate's clerk who owes her a favor. Beat: grief and alliance kindling together.

chapters.title: The Compass Points Inward
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Examining the compass, Juniper finds an engraving inside the case: initials matching both their mother and the company founder. It was a gift between them—evidence of intimacy, not just crime. Beat: betrayal deepens; the enemy knew their family.

chapters.title: Wren Closes In
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Wren's cold efficiency at the office, then Juniper's dread as Wren questions neighbors about a missing child. Beat: the net tightening; Juniper must move Sefa tonight or lose everything.

chapters.title: The Salt House
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper hides Sefa with Maren in the salt-drying house and copies the ledger page, splitting the evidence. Beat: tenderness between Juniper and Sefa; for one evening they are simply family, not fugitives.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: Customs House
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Disguised as a courier, Juniper carries the copy through customs, nearly undone when a guard recognizes the company seal on their old papers. Beat: terror and improvisation; the copy gets through, barely, but the original remains exposed.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reflects on twenty years of complicity—divers who saw, said nothing, drowned anyway. She decides to testify despite her bad heart. Beat: moral awakening; the theme of inheritance as choice, not blood alone.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The company burns its pre-1880 ledgers publicly, 'for hygiene.' Juniper watches the original evidence's context turn to ash and understands the archive checkpoint is now the only place a duplicate exists. Beat: despair transmuting into urgency.

chapters.title: The Founder's Daughter
chapters.summary: New POV: Odile Meridian, the founder's estranged daughter, reads a copied page slipped to her anonymously (by Juniper). She recognizes her father's hand—and her own childhood compass. Beat: reluctant conscience stirring inside the enemy's house.

chapters.title: Bargain at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Juniper and Odile meet secretly on the tidal flats. Odile will unlock the archive if Juniper destroys the page naming her father after the magistrate sees it. Juniper refuses to let any of it vanish again. Beat: uneasy truce; trust tested at the waterline.

chapters.title: Sefa Taken
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Wren seizes Sefa from the salt house, intending to indenture her before midnight—erasing her like her mother was erased. Beat: rage and guilt; every silence Juniper ever kept comes due at once.

chapters.title: The Long Swim
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper dives the company's underwater intake channel at night—skills inherited from the mother they mourned—to reach the compound interior. Beat: the body remembers what the mind was forced to forget; inheritance becomes salvation.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Archive
chapters.summary: Juniper and Odile's alternating POV. Inside the archive, they find the duplicate register confirming decades of live write-offs. Wren catches them; Odile turns her key against her father's men. Beat: climax of nerve—lock turning, lantern light, held breath.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Magistrate's
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Through riot-adjacent New Year crowds, Juniper runs the documents to the magistrate's clerk as fireworks begin. Wren pursues; Maren's testimony arrives by hired chair. Beat: breathless race against the calendar itself.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs converging. At 12:00, the magistrate accepts the filings; warrants issue against the founder's estate. Sefa is released into Maren's care pending kinship claims. Beat: catharsis—the old century's debts formally entered into the new one's books.

chapters.title: Forget the Face No Longer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper speaks their mother's full name aloud at the shoreline where she was 'lost,' the compass in hand. Sefa asks what her mother looked like; Juniper describes her without flinching. Beat: mourning completed; memory reclaimed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Free Water
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Contract dissolved by the magistrate's order, Juniper signs onto an independent diving crew taking Sefa and Maren north. Final image: open water, no company flag, a compass kept not for direction but remembrance. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
